name: zscore_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY at 5-second resolution, a 60-bar rolling window (5 minutes) of price data provides a continuously updating local mean and standard deviation. When NIFTY's current price deviates more than 2.0 standard deviations from this 5-minute rolling mean, it indicates a short-term overextension that is statistically likely to revert. This is fundamentally DIFFERENT from VWAP reversion (strategies v18 and v19) in two critical ways: (1) VWAP is anchored to session open and accumulates all volume since 09:15 — it reflects the session-level fair value and becomes increasingly stable as the day progresses. The rolling mean resets continuously, reflecting only the last 5 minutes of NIFTY price action, making it responsive to RECENT volatility shifts. (2) VWAP deviations on NIFTY are measured against a volume-weighted anchor that institutional TWAP/VWAP algos actively trade toward, creating a structural reversion force. Rolling z-score reversion relies on a different mechanism: short-horizon mean reversion caused by market-maker inventory management. When NIFTY moves 2+ sigma from its 5-minute mean, market makers who delta-hedge option positions accumulate inventory against the move. Their subsequent inventory flattening (selling after accumulating long, or covering after going short) pulls price back toward the recent mean. The 5-minute window is optimal on NIFTY because it approximately matches the inventory cycle of NSE market makers — they typically flatten their delta within 3-7 minutes of accumulation. Earlier in the session, when VWAP has only 30-60 minutes of data, the rolling z-score provides a more stable and responsive reversion signal than session VWAP.

indicators.name: rolling_mean_60
indicators.purpose: Simple moving average over 60 five-second bars = 5 minutes of NIFTY price data. This is the local fair-value estimate. 60 bars chosen because on NIFTY, 5 minutes captures approximately 2-3 full micro-cycles of price oscillation during normal trading. Shorter windows (30 bars/2.5 min) produce a mean that chases price too closely, reducing z-score extremes to below 1.5 and generating no signals. Longer windows (120 bars/10 min) behave too much like session VWAP, losing the 'recent volatility adaptation' that distinguishes this strategy.

indicators.name: rolling_std_60
indicators.purpose: Rolling standard deviation over the same 5-minute window. Critically, this adapts to NIFTY's intraday volatility regime in near-real-time. In a quiet midday session, std might be 3-4 spot points; in a volatile morning, it could be 15-20. A 2-sigma deviation automatically scales: 6-8 points in quiet markets vs 30-40 points in volatile ones. This self-scaling is the key advantage over fixed-point deviation thresholds.

indicators.name: zscore_60
indicators.purpose: Standardized deviation from 5-minute rolling mean. The 2.0 threshold is chosen because on NIFTY 5s data, z-scores above 2.0 occur roughly 5-10 times per session and revert to below 1.0 within 30-90 seconds approximately 60% of the time. Z-scores above 2.5 are rarer but revert more reliably (65-70%); however, they also indicate potential trend days where reversion fails spectacularly, so 2.0 provides the best frequency-accuracy balance.

indicators.name: zscore_velocity
indicators.purpose: Rate of change of z-score over 3 bars (15 seconds). When z-score exceeds 2.0 but zscore_velocity is turning back toward zero (becoming less negative for buy, less positive for sell), it signals the overextension is already starting to revert. This is the timing indicator — it prevents entering while the extension is still deepening. 3-bar lookback is 15 seconds, chosen because NIFTY's initial reversion impulse from market-maker inventory flattening becomes visible within 10-20 seconds of peak overextension.

indicators.name: rolling_mean_slope
indicators.purpose: Slope of the rolling mean over 12 bars (1 minute). If the mean itself is trending strongly (slope > 0.02%/minute), NIFTY is in a trending micro-regime where 2-sigma deviations are more likely to mark trend acceleration than overextension. This filter prevents taking reversion trades during genuine NIFTY trend moves. The 0.02% threshold represents approximately 5 spot points per minute, above which NIFTY is in 'trend mode' not 'mean-reversion mode.'

conditions: zscore_60 < -2.0 (NIFTY is 2+ standard deviations below its 5-minute rolling mean — overextended to the downside)
zscore_velocity > 0 (z-score is turning back toward zero — initial reversion has begun, not still falling)
abs(rolling_mean_slope) < 0.02 (5-minute mean is not trending strongly — confirms mean-reversion regime, not trend)
india_vix < 25 (in high-VIX, z-score extremes persist longer and revert less reliably on NIFTY)
buy_ce.confirmation: zscore_60 crosses above -1.8 from below -2.0 (reversion past initial threshold — momentum toward mean is confirmed)

conditions: zscore_60 > 2.0 (NIFTY 2+ standard deviations above 5-minute rolling mean)

exit.stop_rationale: 5 option points = roughly 10 NIFTY spot points. If the z-score reversion thesis is correct, price should move back toward the rolling mean (z-score approaching 0). A 10-spot-point move FURTHER from the mean after we entered means the overextension is not reverting — NIFTY is trending through the 2-sigma level toward 3-sigma, which on a 5-minute window represents a genuine directional move (news event, large institutional order). 5 points gives room for the 2-3 point noise oscillation near extremes without requiring us to ride a potential 3-sigma blowout.
exit.target_rationale: A reversion from z-score of -2.0 to 0 (full mean reversion) on NIFTY's 5-minute window represents a move of roughly 2 * rolling_std spot points. With typical NIFTY 5-minute std of 8-15 points, full reversion is 16-30 spot points = 8-15 option points. Target of 7 captures approximately half of full reversion (z-score from -2.0 to roughly -1.0), which is the high-probability portion. The second half of reversion (z-score -1.0 to 0) is lower probability as price approaches equilibrium and new directional flow can restart. 7:5 reward-to-risk provides adequate edge at 58%+ win rate.

filters.vix_filter: india_vix < 25 — above 25, NIFTY's intraday distribution develops fatter tails, meaning 2-sigma events are more common but less mean-reverting (they often mark the start of a trend leg, not a reversal)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:20 (need 60 bars = 5 minutes of data for rolling statistics to stabilize) or after 15:10 (closing dynamics distort rolling stats)
filters.volume_filter: none — z-score is a pure price signal; volume adds noise on 5s NIFTY data
filters.trend_filter: rolling_mean_slope < 0.02% — critical filter that distinguishes mean-reversion regimes from trending regimes on NIFTY

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — z-score reversion is well-known in quant finance, but the specific 5-minute rolling window on NIFTY 5s with trend-slope filter provides differentiation from generic implementations

adaptation_notes: Original used 60-bar lookback on 1-min (1 hour) with z-score threshold of 2.0 on individual NIFTY 100 stocks, holding 10-40 minutes. Adapted to NIFTY index at 5s: (1) Lookback preserved at 60 bars but the TIME window compressed from 60 minutes to 5 minutes because the mean-reversion mechanism at play is different: on 1-min stocks, the 1-hour z-score captures intraday overreaction from retail flow; on 5s NIFTY, the 5-minute z-score captures market-maker inventory cycles, which operate on a 3-7 minute timescale. (2) Hold time compressed from 10-40 minutes to 20-90 seconds — market-maker-driven reversion on NIFTY completes within 1-2 minutes. (3) Added rolling_mean_slope filter (absent from original) — critical because at 5-minute windows, a trending NIFTY will show persistent z-score extremes that don't revert. The slope filter avoids these regime-mismatch trades. (4) Z-score velocity lookback reduced from 5 bars on 1-min (5 minutes) to 3 bars on 5s (15 seconds) — the turning point in z-score is visible faster at 5s resolution. (5) VIX filter retained at 25 but reasoning is NIFTY-specific: above VIX 25, NIFTY option market makers widen their quotes and reduce delta-hedging frequency, weakening the inventory-flattening reversion mechanism. (6) Hurst exponent filter from original dropped — computationally expensive and not meaningful on a single-instrument (NIFTY) 5-minute window; replaced by the simpler rolling_mean_slope filter which captures the same regime-detection intent. (7) Stop/target set to 5/7 option points matching the typical 2-sigma to 1-sigma reversion on NIFTY's 5-minute rolling statistics.
weaknesses: 60 bars of 5s data = only 5 minutes — the rolling standard deviation is estimated from just 60 observations, making it statistically noisy; a few outlier bars can dramatically shift the z-score threshold
Mean-reversion regime assumption fails on event-driven days (RBI announcement, global shock) where NIFTY trends persistently through z-score extremes
The 5-minute rolling mean 'chases' price during trends, which can mask the true extent of overextension — price may be 50 points from the session VWAP but only 2 sigma from the rolling mean

Similarity risk with VWAP reversion strategies: although the mechanism is different (rolling mean vs VWAP), both are counter-trend strategies that will fire on the same moves, leading to correlated drawdowns in a multi-strategy portfolio
